# Harness Summary

The in-context learning approach struggles across all three validation sets, with performance degrading as problem complexity and context size increase. On ds_alpha (small, 60.4% eval accuracy), the model achieves moderate performance but shows inverted accuracy (35.7% train vs. 60.4% eval), suggesting it isn't effectively learning from training examples. On ds_beta (large context with 14-way multiple choice, 29.2% eval accuracy), performance collapses to near-random guessing despite 30K-character prompts, indicating that larger context windows and more examples don't help. On ds_gamma (intermediate size, metrics incomplete but showing consistent failures), the same pattern emerges with the model selecting plausible-sounding answers without capturing underlying patterns.

**Recurring failure pattern**: All predictions use identical reasoning format ("Closest demonstrations suggest...") and frequently pick semantically similar but incorrect answers, indicating the model is doing shallow similarity matching rather than learning the actual problem-solving logic.

**Key issues for improvement**: (1) The approach doesn't scale—performance worsens with dataset size and context, suggesting prompt engineering alone won't solve this; (2) training-evaluation disconnect in ds_alpha indicates the learning mechanism itself is broken; (3) context bloat provides no benefit, wasting tokens without improving reasoning.
